newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Eight more charged in S.Korean graft scandal.
newsitem.headline: Eight more charged in S.Korean graft scandal.

text.p: The mayor of South Korea's second largest city, Pusan, and seven serving or former lawmakers were charged on Thursday with taking bribes from the founder of the scandal-hit Hanbo Group.
The eight were among 33 politicians named by the Hanbo founder as having accepted his money, chief prosecutor Shim Je-ryoon told reporters.

Hanbo's patriach Chung Tae-soo, 74, is on trial with 10 other people on charges of bribing top politicians and bankers to secure credit for his steelmaking flagship, which collapsed in January under debts of five trillion won ($5.6 billion).
"I regret we could not indict all the other politicians," Shim said.
He explained that the others had only escaped indictment because of a legal loophole giving politicians immunity from prosecution for receiving money during an election.
Pusan mayor Moon Jung-soo was charged with accepting kickbacks of 200 million won ($224,000) before he became mayor of the southern port city in 1995, Shim said.
He alleged that Hanbo's founder handed the cash to Moon in an apple crate.

Among the seven others charged, but not physically detained, were two serving lawmakers -- Kim Sang-hyun of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, and Ro Seung-woo of the ruling New Korea Party.
The remainder were former lawmakers from both the ruling and opposition camps, Shim said.

On Wednesday, a presidential Blue House official said 70 high-level officials were under investigation for corruption. Domestic media said they included several cabinet ministers, vice ministers and heads of local governments.
Last Saturday, President Kim Young-sam's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, was arrested on charges of accepting kickbacks worth millions of dollars and evading taxes.

Opposition parties have alleged that Hanbo founder Chung helped bankroll the president's 1992 election victory, and that Kim Hyun-chul laundered huge sums of leftover funds through his business cronies.
One of the 33 politicians on Chung's list -- which sent shockwaves through South Korean political circles -- was Kim Soo-han, the speaker of the National Assembly. He was not indicted. ($1=890 won)
